title: Merrick Road: Ancient South Shore Trail
summary: Local histories describe Merrick Road, once known as South Country Road, as following an older Indigenous footpath or forest trail across the south shore. The route linked waterways, settlements, planting areas, and neighboring communities before English road-building fixed it into the colonial landscape.
address_label: Merrick Road / South Country Road corridor, Freeport-Baldwin-Merrick area
ancestral_territory_note: Linked to Merrick Ancestral Land as a south shore travel corridor.
why_this_matters: Merrick Road shows how everyday infrastructure can preserve traces of older Native geographies. Seen as a south shore travel corridor, the road carries histories of movement, exchange, and connection across Merrick ancestral land.
introduction_title: A Road Following an Older Route
introduction_content: The modern road corridor preserves continuity between Indigenous movement, colonial travel, and today's everyday route.
